## Summary

Protect dtplyr typed Grouping selections and Nest preparation from caller `head()` and generated `[` bindings.

```text
immutable root -> isolated zero-row schema
derived query  -> faithful base function dispatch
               -> existing safe-metadata refusal before caller code otherwise
```

Closes #1303.
Closes #1326.

## Evidence

- **Before:** an immutable root could send both source rows to caller `head()`, lose character Grouping dimensions, or mutate the caller table. A derived query could call caller `[` on empty input and infer different types from native collection.
  **After:** public regressions cover typed dimensions/fixed keys, both Nest verbs and cell partitions, name-only inspection, native collection, and caller values. Ordinary non-functions in function lookup retain base dispatch; active/lazy/custom bindings remain refused before execution.
- **Review-ready full:** `030834a868d7ab6f338e014746e256a02af30c7a`; 237 files, 216791 assertions, no failures/warnings/skips; source-tarball check 0 ERROR / 0 WARNING / 0 NOTE. [Verification and timing disposition](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1333#issuecomment-6651357272).
- **Review:** separate gpt-6.1-sol / xhigh Standards and Spec reviewers. Both initial findings fixed in 030834a8; follow-up reports zero new findings on either axis. [Review and dispositions](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1333#issuecomment-6651384805).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revertible code and test changes; no data migration.

**Blast Radius:** dtplyr

Typed Grouping inspection and shared Margin preparation. Caller-table preservation and ADR 0020's source-processing boundary remain enforced.

## Standards

Zero documented-standard violations; one baseline judgement call.
Possible Duplicated Code: test-dtplyr-bracket-metadata repeats the identical caller-bracket fixture in the first two tests; the identical Nest normalizer also appears in bracket/root metadata files. A narrowly scoped shared fixture/helper can give these behaviors one home while keeping separate public-interface assertions.
Disposition: accepted as test cleanup; follow-up implementation pending.

## Spec

One P2 finding: preserve base dispatch through ordinary non-function bracket bindings. The first-binding identity check in dtplyr_base_binding returns FALSE for a normal binding such as `[` <- NULL. R function lookup skips non-functions, so native derived collection uses base `[`, and faithful types are safely available. Typed inspection and both Nest verbs currently refuse.
Requirement: #1326 acceptance, "Retain name-only inspection, base-dispatch typed metadata, and explicit native collection behavior."
Disposition: accepted. Continue lookup past ordinary non-function values while preserving refusal before active binding lookup, promise forcing, or custom function execution. Add regression coverage for base dispatch through non-function bindings. Follow-up implementation pending.

Summary: Standards 0 hard violations / 1 judgement call; Spec 1 finding (P2). No other missing requirements, scope creep or incorrect implementations found. This record certifies only the reviewed snapshot, not a future fix.

## Follow-up review

The [initial review](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1333#issuecomment-6650959501) covers the unchanged behavior.

Standards and Spec reviewers each ran in a fresh, independent context with **gpt-6.1-sol / xhigh**. Both rounds were read-only.

## Standards

**Zero new documented-standard violations; zero new baseline smell findings.**

The initial Duplicated Code judgement is resolved in [030834a8](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/commit/030834a868d7ab6f338e014746e256a02af30c7a): `helper-dtplyr-metadata-fixtures.R` owns the shared caller-bracket fixture and Nest-result normalizer, retaining the separate public-interface assertions.

## Spec

**Zero new findings:** no missing/partial requirement, scope creep or incorrect implementation identified in the new behavior.

The initial P2 is fixed in the same commit. `dtplyr_base_binding()` skips ordinary non-functions and checks the first function, preserving refusal before active/lazy bindings, missing formals or custom functions. The public regressions in `test-dtplyr-bracket-metadata.R` cover direct/inherited NULL/numeric bindings for `[` and `+`, typed dimensions/fixed keys, name-only inspection, native collection, both Nest verbs and caller-table integrity; inherited unsafe bindings behind NULL remain refused. These acceptance assertions fail with the previous first-binding comparison.

Summary: Standards **0 new** / Spec **0 new**; both accepted initial findings are resolved. The initial and follow-up records identify their separate snapshots; published history was preserved.
